layout: Two columns, five biome rows: plains, forest, islands, swamp, mountains
town: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent sprite atlas for a dark fantasy regional strategy map, painted pixel RTS terrain art with fine irregular pixel clusters, muted parchment earth, charcoal outlines, warm upper-left lighting. High bird's-eye oblique view from VERY FAR AWAY, around 65 degrees down, no horizon, no perspective convergence. Each building is TINY relative to the whole town, many small roofs and narrow lanes, not an oversized castle icon. Consistent world scale and camera for all pieces. True transparent background, no labels, no grid lines, no text, no pedestal, no rectangular terrain patches. Exactly TWO columns and FIVE rows of separate assets, evenly spaced equal cells with ample transparent gutters. Each asset fully contained with no clipped pixels. Rows top to bottom: plains, forest, islands, swamp, mountains. Each cell is one complete modest town footprint, wide and low, with 25-45 very tiny buildings, a few low enclosure walls, streets and open spaces. Small individual houses no more than 1/15 town width; central hall no more than 1/6 width. LEFT column player settlement with restrained old gold pennants and ochre roof accents. RIGHT column independent market town with subdued teal awnings around an open trading square, no large citadel. Plains row: farm town, straw/brown roofs, dusty ochre lanes, low stone walls. Forest row: dark timber woodland town with moss roofs, a few surrounding tree crowns at the SAME small scale, irregular clearing. Islands row: pale stone coastal town, slate roofs, tiny boat sheds and dry quays but NO water painted into sprite; compact irregular shoreline-compatible footprint. Swamp row: tiny stilt hamlets, dark plum-grey roofs, narrow timber walkways, sparse tawny rushes, no forest canopy, NO painted pools. Mountains row: many low reddish slate and stone houses on stepped rocky terraces, tiny retaining walls, dusty rose stone. Outer edges must break into a few scattered tiny buildings, grass and stones with transparent gaps. Focus roofs, street network and collective settlement silhouette, not readable individual windows or doors. No giant towers, trees, banners or characters. Enough subtle source colour variation to preserve materials without biome-wide tinting.

Production transparent sprite atlas for a dark fantasy regional strategy map, painted pixel RTS terrain art with fine irregular pixel clusters, muted parchment earth, charcoal outlines, warm upper-left lighting. High bird's-eye oblique view from VERY FAR AWAY, around 65 degrees down, no horizon, no perspective convergence. Each building is TINY relative to the whole town, many small roofs and narrow lanes, not an oversized castle icon. Consistent world scale and camera for all pieces. True transparent background, no labels, no grid lines, no text, no pedestal, no rectangular terrain patches. Exactly TWO columns and FIVE rows of separate assets, evenly spaced equal cells with ample transparent gutters. Each asset fully contained with no clipped pixels. Rows top to bottom: plains, forest, islands, swamp, mountains. Each cell is a small composable OUTSKIRTS terrain piece, approximately half a town footprint, sparse and low, seen at the same distant scale as many tiny town roofs. LEFT column productive district; RIGHT column road-entry district. Plains: narrow strip fields with tiny barns / a forked dirt approach through hedges and low dry-stone walls. Forest: timber yards and very small woodcutters huts among sparse tiny trees / irregular clearing with low palisade gap, branching paths and stumps. Islands: dry fishery yard with tiny sheds nets and stones / pale stone quay approach and broken rubble paths, NO painted water, no beach-shaped base. Swamp: short raised boardwalks and tiny peat drying sheds in plum peat and gold rushes / branching timber causeway with small reed clumps and muddy root banks, no water backdrop. Mountains: thin terraced gardens and tiny miners sheds with rosy rubble / stepped stone approach passing low retaining walls and scree. These are feathered broken terrain decals with genuine transparent gaps between components, not oval badges or little landscape scenes. No large buildings, no castles, no text. Keep paths entering lower centre and branching toward left and right, open ends that can overlap other assets.
